chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, from Abul-Husayn al-Khadim (the pearl seller), from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

My father asked him while I was present: 'When is the affair of an orphan permitted (i.e., when does he attain legal majority)?' He replied: 'Until he reaches his ashud (full strength/maturity).' He asked: 'And what is his ashud?' He replied: 'Al-ihlatam (seminal emission).' He said: 'I said: The boy may be eighteen years old, or less, or more, and not have a seminal emission?' He replied: 'When he reaches the age (thirteen) and the matter is written upon him, his affair is permitted, unless he is a safih (foolish/impulsive) or weak (in mind).'
ai.seo_question: When does an orphan attain legal majority in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal clarifies the criteria for a boy's legal majority (bulugh) in Shia jurisprudence, establishing that while seminal emission is the primary sign of maturity, reaching the age of thirteen serves as the definitive chronological threshold. The ruling remains contingent upon the individual's mental capacity, excluding those deemed safih (impulsive) or weak-minded from managing their affairs independently. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on combining biological markers with cognitive competence in determining legal responsibility.
